The degree of medium modification characterizes the hot QCD matter in the deconfined phase, and this effect emerges in principle from thermal QCD, though different approximation schemes yield consistent results. Gluon radiation has also been considered in the context of gluon density saturation in the initial stage, where a strongly interacting gluonic atmosphere is crucial for rapid local thermalization. The time evolution of the RHIC fireball influences observable particle production spectra, and given a strong initial interaction, the resulting state is modeled as a relativistic fluid undergoing hydrodynamic flow, for which generalized fluid mechanics characterizing the long-distance transport of color charges has been developed. The authors previously discovered single skyrmion solutions in color fluid and found an expanding skyrmion case consistent with the expanding nature of the RHIC fireball. The pattern of gluon radiation pertaining to the color current of these non-static configurations is an important characteristic, motivating the calculation of the radiation spectrum in a semiclassical approach. The main results are a fast fall-off in the ultraviolet side of the spectrum, a smooth peak dominating the intermediate energy, and a long tail in the infrared. The equation of state is approximated as epsilon = 3p, describing radiation, and the free energy density is obtained by integrating the ideal fluid formula. The expanding soliton solution is specified with a scale R(t) and a small parameter lambda = tau/R0. The semiclassical amplitude is computed using the lowest-order interaction between the classical current and a free quantum gluon field, and the radiation spectrum is derived from the density of states and energy distribution. The numerical results are presented for lambda = 1/15, 2/15, and 1/5, showing the density of states and energy spectrum as functions of kappa. The comparison with other approaches reveals differences in the infrared behavior, which stems from the medium size being characterized by the soliton size R0 rather than being infinitely large. The hydrodynamical approach also opens possibilities for addressing the eccentricity of the elliptic flow, which will be the topic of follow-up work. draft_summary.title: Gluon Radiation of an Expanding Color Skyrmion in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
draft_summary.executive_summary: This letter investigates gluon radiation emitted during the hydrodynamic stage of deconfined hot QCD matter, or quark-gluon plasma (QGP), which is central to interpreting relativistic heavy-ion collisions at RHIC. The medium-induced radiation has been extensively studied in the context of final-state partonic energy loss, or jet quenching, where spatially extended nuclear matter affects the fragmentation and hadronization of hard partons, and essentially all high transverse-momentum hadronic observables are affected at collider energies. The degree of medium modification characterizes the hot QCD matter in the deconfined phase, and this effect emerges in principle from thermal QCD, though different approximation schemes yield consistent results. Gluon radiation has also been considered in the context of gluon density saturation in the initial stage, where a strongly interacting gluonic atmosphere is crucial for rapid local thermalization. The time evolution of the RHIC fireball influences observable particle production spectra, and given a strong initial interaction, the resulting state is modeled as a relativistic fluid undergoing hydrodynamic flow, for which generalized fluid mechanics characterizing the long-distance transport of color charges has been developed. The authors previously discovered single skyrmion solutions in color fluid and found an expanding skyrmion case consistent with the expanding nature of the RHIC fireball. The pattern of gluon radiation pertaining to the color current of these non-static configurations is an important characteristic, motivating the calculation of the radiation spectrum in a semiclassical approach. The main results are a fast fall-off in the ultraviolet side of the spectrum, a smooth peak dominating the intermediate energy, and a long tail in the infrared. The paper reviews nonabelian fluid mechanics, calculates the nonabelian current for the soliton solution, computes the semiclassical gluon radiation, and compares the spectrum with other approaches. The color current is derived from a nonlinear sigma model in a first-order formalism, with the configuration described by a group element field U and velocity field omega. The equation of state is approximated as epsilon = 3p, describing radiation, and the free energy density is obtained by integrating the ideal fluid formula. The expanding soliton solution is specified with a scale R(t) and a small parameter lambda = tau/R0. The semiclassical amplitude is computed using the lowest-order interaction between the classical current and a free quantum gluon field, and the radiation spectrum is derived from the density of states and energy distribution. The numerical results are presented for lambda = 1/15, 2/15, and 1/5, showing the density of states and energy spectrum as functions of kappa. The comparison with other approaches reveals differences in the infrared behavior, which stems from the medium size being characterized by the soliton size R0 rather than being infinitely large. The hydrodynamical approach also opens possibilities for addressing the eccentricity of the elliptic flow, which will be the topic of follow-up work. The work was supported by a CUNY Collaborative Research Incentive grant, and the author benefited from mentoring by V. P. Nair.
